analysis.investment_thesis: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings is a Murugappa Group franchise compounding net profit at 16.7% CAGR over 9 years with recent acceleration (27.5% EBITDA CAGR over 3 years), trading at a compelling P/E of 13.0 and forward P/E of 10.73 — implying a PEG ratio below 1 for a business with proven management depth and a diversifying loan book. The combination of India's underpenetrated credit market, a trusted brand in vehicle finance, and Murugappa Group governance makes this the most Fisher-consistent name in this set.
key_strengths: Net profit growing consistently: INR 2,239 Cr (FY22) → INR 2,810 Cr → INR 3,851 Cr → INR 4,740 Cr (FY25), compounding at ~28% over 3 years
Forward P/E of 10.73 for a business growing profits at 17-28% implies significant mispricing; PEG is well below 1.0
Murugappa Group pedigree provides management depth, governance standards, and long-term capital allocation discipline — qualities I weight heavily
key_risks: D/E of 6.35 is very high; while structurally normal for an NBFC, it creates vulnerability in a credit cycle or funding cost spike
Total debt of INR 1,74,366 Cr against equity of INR 13,670 Cr means any asset quality deterioration in vehicle/SME/consumer loans will flow directly to equity
Revenue CAGR of 17.1% over 9 years is solid but includes a highly irregular year in FY17 (INR 2,688 Cr); the business model has evolved considerably and historical comparisons are imperfect
red_flags: OCF has been negative all 5 recent years (inherent to NBFC loan-book expansion), which requires continuous external funding and makes the business sensitive to capital market conditions
ROCE of 10.6% is below my preferred 20% threshold; NBFC economics inherently depress this metric versus non-financial businesses
DII concentration at 26% with FII at 13.8% means institutional selling could cause disproportionate price pressure
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cholamandalam Financial Holdings is the holding entity for Chola Finance (vehicle loans, home loans, SME credit) and Chola MS General Insurance — both quality franchises in India's structurally underpenetrated credit market. What I find most compelling is the recent profit acceleration (net profit nearly doubled from INR 2,239 Cr in FY22 to INR 4,740 Cr in FY25) at a time when the stock still trades at just 13x earnings. The Murugappa Group has a 75-year track record of building durable businesses — this is the kind of management continuity and institutional integrity I look for in my Scuttlebutt process.

The negative OCF is the most common question I receive on NBFC holding companies, and it reflects loan disbursements being classified as operating outflows — not a cash burn in the economic sense. What matters for Chola is net interest margin stability, asset quality trends, and the pace of geographic and product expansion, all of which appear healthy given the profit trajectory. At a forward P/E of 10.73 for a business compounding profits at 17–28%, the margin of safety is adequate for a long-term position.
